newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar hints at Suria, MBf merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar hints at Suria, MBf merger plan.

text.p: Malaysian acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim hinted on Monday of a merger between financial groups Suria Capital Bhd and MBf Capital Bhd .

"On the Suria-MBf Capital merger, I am not in a position to comment on anything because I have not seen the proposals, the national Bernama news agency quoted Anwar as saying, when asked to comment on a possible merger between Suria and MBf Capital.
"However I was told that it has been sent to either the Treasury or Central Bank," added Anwar.
Anwar said merger proposals, especially those involving state interests and agencies, must be in the interest of many and not just one or two businessmen.
"The reason is that we must protect the interest of the state or the agency," he told reporters after opening an energy conference.

Stock market rumours of a merger between Suria, which is controlled by the eastern Sabah state government, and MBf Capital in the last two months, have boosted the stock of both companies. MBf Capital was suspended from Monday trading, being last traded at 5.20 ringgit.
At the midday break on Monday, Suria surged 27 cents to 3.04 ringgit.
Bernama said Sabah's Ministry of Finance had also issued a statement saying follow up discussions were needed after both parties had received approval from the central bank.

"Warisan Harta Sabah Sdn Bhd, the state's wholly-owned subsidiary, is seeking the Ministry of Finance's approval to proceed with negotiations involving its subsidiary, Suria Capital. Warisan Harta has already submitted its proposal to the Central Bank," the statement said.
Officials at both companies were not immediately available for comment.
A source close to the negotiations told Reuters earlier on Monday that both companies have submitted a proposal to start negotiating a merger to the Malaysian authorities.
